## Review (independent reviewer)

Verdict: sound to land. Nothing High; two Medium points for the lead, the rest Low.

- **Database (0026).** The trigger (`0026_game_given_format.sql:29-47`) refuses any change of `given_format` once the OLD row has `format_fixed_at` or is live, final or forfeit; the constraint (`:20-23`) asks only a versioned document of at most 16 KB, not its shape (the contracts check that; an unreadable one falls back to the season's, `season-rules-of.ts:54`). Low: one update setting `status = 'live'` and `given_format` together passes the trigger; no path does. Check and write are one step: both commands take the tracker's own lock (`give-game-format.ts:31`, `clear-game-format.ts:29`, the same `lockLiveGame` as `apply-tracker-commands.ts:184`) and the update repeats every condition with the version (`update-game-given-format.ts:17-28`). Both new queries are fenced (`fence-filter-check` on them: 2 caught, 0 problems). Nullable column, no backfill needed; `schema-types.ts` has it.
- **Rules.** A game starts under the given format, else the season's (`season-rules-of.ts:49-67`, fixed under the lock at `apply-tracker-commands.ts:410-423`); mark not started returns to the given one (`mark-not-started.ts:150`). A format is checked in contracts (`season-rules.ts:262-272`: 2 or 4 periods, 60 to 3600 s, bonus 1 to 30, double bonus after the bonus, stop-clock time within a period, no mercy on a running clock) and parsed strictly by the endpoint (`game-format-endpoint.ts`); "admin" is `games.manage` from the session's context (`game-format.ts:47-56`), never the body.
- **Medium: a second device with the confirmation open keeps the old rules on screen.** The panel reads once (`game-format-panel.tsx:59-67`); only its first taken batch makes it reload (record 062, `tracker-controller.ts:14-18`). The server's box score is right, but the game then has plays, so the new format is never asked about or said on that device (`open-tracker-game.ts:14-17`), and taps queued offline were made on the old clock.
- **Medium (builder 3's a): "Confirm and start scoring" under the open form** (`tracker-opening.tsx:801`) starts the game with what was typed lost, and the form lives only in the confirmation, so there is no way back to it. Suggest hiding or disabling Confirm while the form is open.
- **Low (builder 3's b).** Only the stand-in's data: a real game goes live only through `apply-tracker-commands.ts:410`, which fixes the format. But a real game decided by a final or box score has no format fixed: Games says it follows its season's format, and greys the button with "The game is under way" (`game-format-panel.tsx:147-151`, `game-format.ts:70`) on a game that is over.
- **Low:** the panel never retries a failed read (`game-format-panel.tsx:61-62`): the admin page stays on "reading".
- **Screens.** All text in `messages/en/tracker.ts`; said back in one line, "Saved for this game only: …" (B2, B4); presets change this game only.
- **Tests.** No `.catch` swallows (`game-format-test.mjs:334,344` rethrow with the page's text), every wait has the 30 s limit, no check reads back only what the test set. Low: the clock is never run, so "the clock follows" is the starting 8:00 of Q1 and Q2 (`:242,274,288`); an admin with the setting off is proved in core tests only.
- **Spec.** P7 §5.1 and T3 say what the code does. Low: the checklist B1 to B4 the plan names is nowhere in `docs/specs/v1` (searched), so the form, presets, said-back line and greyed button are not in the spec. Pending T-340 to T-343 and S-93: 4 cells each, as their tables, no `|` in a cell; `tests/pending-decisions.test.mjs` passes (11).
- **Runs, all passed:** `game-format-test` (33), `scoring-plays-test` (709), `scoring-screen-test` (1002), and the chain after `score-this-game-test` from `scoring-trouble-test` to `undo-removing-test` (17 tests in three chunks); vitest of the 0026 schema test, the three commands, the endpoint and `tracker-controller-format` (6 files, 19 tests). Not run: `scorekeepers-test` (builder 3 ran it); the whole fence check did not finish in 580 s.
